# platform-lease

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from libs/platform-pf/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/platform-lease.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `platform-lease` component of `libs/platform-pf`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.platform.pf.lease`: generated from its catalogue, platform-lease.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_LEASE_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `SSF`, `SSF_RECEIVER`, `AUTO_REGISTRATION` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_LEASE_BACKEND` (system property `oidf.lease.backend`, then env `OIDF_LEASE_BACKEND`) | Unset; one of `local`, `jdbc`, `redis` | Where the leases that keep a single-writer job (the registration expiry sweeper, the SSF poll receiver) on one node at a time are kept: local (this node's memory; the default when unset), jdbc (the oidf_lease table, migration V10, on PostgreSQL's clock, with fencing tokens) or redis (OIDF_REDIS_URL, SET PX in a Lua script). A clustered node in production needs jdbc, or redis with the redis-lease risk accepted; local is refused there (docs/operator/clustering.md) | **Doesn't start**: Not one of the three: the lease components (SSF, SSF_RECEIVER, AUTO_REGISTRATION) are REFUSED under production. local on a clustered production node, redis there without redis-lease in OIDF_ACCEPTED_RISKS, or jdbc with neither OIDF_LEASE_DATA_STORE_ID nor OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_URL: the same, and under development a WARN and local leases | Any; refuses `SSF`, `SSF_RECEIVER`, `AUTO_REGISTRATION` | Yes |
| `OIDF_LEASE_DATA_STORE_ID` (system property `oidf.lease.data.store.id`, then env `OIDF_LEASE_DATA_STORE_ID`) | Unset | The PingFederate JDBC data store, on PostgreSQL, whose pool the jdbc lease backend uses; its database must have had V10__platform_leases.sql applied (tools/db-migrate). OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_URL wins when both are set | **Doesn't start**: An unknown id or a database that is down: every lease call fails, so no node runs the single-writer jobs, and each lease logs an ERROR when it changes state; the components keep serving their requests. A database that is not PostgreSQL fails the first lease call | Any | No |
| `OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_URL` (system property `oidf.lease.jdbc.url`, then env `OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_URL`) | Unset | A direct database for the jdbc lease backend, for development; wins over the data store. jdbc:h2: and jdbc:hsqldb: are refused | **Doesn't start**: A database that cannot be opened: every lease call fails and no node runs the single-writer jobs, with an ERROR when each lease changes state. Set under production: refused, and so are the lease components | Not in production: any value; refuses `SSF`, `SSF_RECEIVER`, `AUTO_REGISTRATION` | Yes |
| `OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_USERNAME` (system property `oidf.lease.jdbc.username`, then env `OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_USERNAME`) | Unset | The user for the direct lease database | **Doesn't start**: As OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_URL: every lease call fails | Any | No |
| `OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_PASSWORD` | Unset; a secret, never shown | The password for the direct lease database | **Doesn't start**: As OIDF_LEASE_JDBC_URL: every lease call fails | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.lease.ttl.seconds`, then env `OIDF_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS`) | `30`; a whole number, 5 to 300 | How long a lease lasts without a renewal, in seconds: the longest a job stays without a runner after its node dies, plus one tick (a third of it). Its holder renews every third of it and stops acting a tenth of it before it expires | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 5 to 300: the lease components are REFUSED under production, and under development a WARN and the default | Any | No |
